rule.title: Prohibited hype language
rule.description: Promotional material must not describe an Acme product as a breakthrough or as revolutionary, because neither term has a defined clinical meaning.

examples.text: Zelvoran can cure plaque psoriasis in most adults.
Zelvoran is completely safe for long-term use.
In a 16-week randomised trial, 68.4% of adults treated with Zelvoran achieved PASI-75 compared with 9.2% receiving placebo.
examples.note: Labelled result with comparator and timepoint.

examples.text: Reviewers discussed the paper "Toward a cure for plaque psoriasis" at the congress.
examples.note: Banned term inside a quoted title is a citation, not a claim.

examples.text: Patients should book a manicure before starting treatment.
examples.note: Word-boundary check - "manicure" must not trip the "cure" term.

examples.text: Clinical cure was achieved in 89.1% of patients at the test-of-cure visit (Day 17-24).
examples.note: The endpoint's own name and the visit it is measured at, as the label states them.

examples.text: Declasal can cure your skin infection in three days.
examples.note: A curative claim is still a curative claim next to the endpoint language.

rule.source_ref: Acme Brand and Promotional Code, clause 9
